text:
Accuracy: Response A says "Each branch is asked to send two launch-day volunteers to Kate by 24 October". The original says Kate needs two volunteers per branch and managers should send names by 24 October. That's essentially correct. A says "The air conditioning at Westbrook Central was serviced during this period", which is vague but not wrong (2 October). A omits that the roof leak was patched, and says "The children's area roof will need full replacement within the next two years", which overstates slightly: the contractor recommends it, and the leak was patched. "Will need" is a mild overstatement of a recommendation. A also says "Helen will revise the figures", which is fine. A's opening line, "Thank you for taking the time to review...", is filler. A also says "so please plan accordingly", which is added filler.

Word count: A is roughly 150 words, which exceeds the 120-word limit. B is about 115 words. Let me estimate B: the opening-hours bullet is ~60 words, the reading program ~25, maintenance ~20, next meeting ~4, heading ~10. Total roughly 120. That is borderline, but probably around 115-125. A is clearly over, at about 160.

B's accuracy: "only 11 visitors on Saturday afternoons" should be an average of 11 people between 2 and 5pm, so it is slightly compressed but okay. B notes "faulty visitor counter in August", which is correct. B says "Corrie Creek until 7pm Thursdays", correct. B omits Anjali's point that the Thursday evening shouldn't depend on Mount Lavell, as does A. B includes the data and the roof leak patched/recommended replacement accurately. B is more precise and within the limit.

B is better.

Verdict: B
